papers.title: Hospital, Patient, and Clinical Factors Influence 30- and 90-Day Readmission After Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The purpose of this study was to analyze the hospital, clinical, and patient factors associated with inpatient readmission after total hip arthroplasty (THA) in the Medicare population and to understand the primary reasons for readmission. METHODS: The Medicare 100% national hospital claims database was used to identify 442,333 older patients (65+) with a primary THA in 3730 hospitals between 2010 and 2013. A multilevel logistic regression analysis with a clustered data structure was used to investigate the risk of all-cause 30- and 90-day readmission, incorporating hospital, clinical, and patient factors. RESULTS: At 30 days, 5.8% (median) of the patients were readmitted, whereas at 90 days, 10.5% (median) were readmitted. Geographic census region, hospital procedure volume, and nonprofit ownership were the only significant hospital factors among those we studied. Overall, clinical factors explained more of the variation in readmission rates than general hospital factors. Use of a perioperative transfusion was associated with 14% greater risk, patients discharged to home had 28% lower risk, and surgeon volume and length of stay were also significant risk factors. The top 5 most frequently reported primary reasons for 30-day readmission in THA were procedure related: dislocation (5.9%), deep infection (5.1%), wound infection (4.8%), periprosthetic fracture (4.4%), or hematoma (3.4%). CONCLUSION: These findings support further optimization of the delivery of care-both intraoperative and postoperative-to reduce the broad variation in hospital readmissions.

llm.relevance_to_user: 这篇论文仅分析全髋关节置换术后再入院的临床因素，未涉及任何生物力学建模或植入物力学评估。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not quantify proximal femur stress/strain, micromotion, or compare intact vs implanted femur; it is a clinical readmission analysis with no finite element or biomechanical modeling.

summary_zh.motivation: 分析全髋关节置换术后30天和90天再入院率的医院、临床和患者因素

summary_en.motivation: To investigate hospital, clinical, and patient factors associated with inpatient readmission after total hip arthroplasty in the Medicare population.
summary_en.method: A multilevel logistic regression analysis was performed on 442,333 primary THA patients from the Medicare 100% national hospital claims database (2010-2013).
summary_en.result: Clinical factors explained more variation in readmission rates than hospital factors; perioperative transfusion increased risk by 14% while discharge to home reduced risk by 28%.
summary_en.validation: Statistical validation using a large national claims database with clustered data structure.

summary_en.motivation: To determine if severe obesity increases infection risk after direct anterior approach total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A retrospective review of 732 patients categorized by BMI groups compared infection rates.
summary_en.result: Severely obese patients had a significantly higher risk of postoperative infection.
summary_en.validation: Clinical retrospective cohort analysis of patient outcomes.
